# Tech Stack Studio

Animated SVG technology stack builder. 542 verified logos, each with its own
motion. Public site: https://thanhnguyxnorg.github.io/Techstack-Studio
Repository: https://github.com/ThanhNguyxnOrg/Techstack-Studio

## What you can generate

1. A README table of animated icon links (markdown).
2. A single animated SVG banner containing several logos.
3. A standalone HTML page with the same banner.

## Machine-readable data

- https://thanhnguyxnorg.github.io/Techstack-Studio/catalog.json — every icon: id, name, category, subcategory, role,
  docsUrl, monogram, brandColor, svg, sourceSvg, concept, technique.
- https://thanhnguyxnorg.github.io/Techstack-Studio/icons/manifest.json — id → motion concept/technique/status.
- https://thanhnguyxnorg.github.io/Techstack-Studio/icons/animated/<id>.svg — the animated icon.
- https://thanhnguyxnorg.github.io/Techstack-Studio/icons/source/<id>.svg — the static icon.

Icon paths in catalog.json are relative to the site root. Ids are lowercase and
punctuation-free: next.js → nextdotjs, vue → vuedotjs, three.js → threedotjs,
socket.io → socketdotio, aws → amazonaws. Use catalog.json instead of guessing.

Every icon carries an aliases array, so resolve a human name before
building a URL (vue → vuedotjs, nodejs → nodedotjs, aws → amazonaws).

## Share link

https://thanhnguyxnorg.github.io/Techstack-Studio/?stack=react,nodedotjs opens the builder with that stack. Aliases such as
nodejs are accepted by the CLI and the share link, but icon files use canonical
ids from catalog.json.

## Build a banner without the UI

```bash
npm run stack -- --ids=react,nodedotjs --out=stack.svg
```

Formats: svg (default), md (README table), html (standalone page). Inside the repo
alternatively: npx tsx scripts/buildStackBanner.ts --ids=...
Add --theme=light --cols=5 --speed=1.5 when needed.

## Paste-ready README snippet

```html
<table>
  <tr>
  <td align="center" width="92"><a href="https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer"><img src="https://thanhnguyxnorg.github.io/Techstack-Studio/icons/animated/javascript.svg" alt="JavaScript" width="48" height="48" /><br /><sub><b>JavaScript</b></sub></a></td>
  <td align="center" width="92"><a href="https://www.typescriptlang.org/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer"><img src="https://thanhnguyxnorg.github.io/Techstack-Studio/icons/animated/typescript.svg" alt="TypeScript" width="48" height="48" /><br /><sub><b>TypeScript</b></sub></a></td>
  <td align="center" width="92"><a href="https://react.dev/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer"><img src="https://thanhnguyxnorg.github.io/Techstack-Studio/icons/animated/react.svg" alt="React" width="48" height="48" /><br /><sub><b>React</b></sub></a></td>
  <td align="center" width="92"><a href="https://www.postgresql.org/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer"><img src="https://thanhnguyxnorg.github.io/Techstack-Studio/icons/animated/postgresql.svg" alt="PostgreSQL" width="48" height="48" /><br /><sub><b>PostgreSQL</b></sub></a></td>
  </tr>
</table>
```

Each icon carries its own animation and a prefers-reduced-motion fallback, so a
static screenshot still looks correct.
